summary: Inspect one tabletop product using stable authored handle frames, one-hand rigid grab and a bounded two-hand transform on the product root, with controller-loss and desktop alternatives explicit.
objective: Inspect one tabletop product using stable authored handle frames, one-hand rigid grab and a bounded two-hand transform on the product root, with controller-loss and desktop alternatives explicit.
intent_signals: Manipulate a product with two XR inputs and equivalent desktop controls.
example_prompts: Build a two-hand XR inspection of a modular camera rig with finite scale clamps and controller-loss handling.
not_for: Force, ergonomics, hand biomechanics or hardware compatibility certification.

entities.name: Product root
entities.guidance: Blender authors one metre-scale product root with stable part/handle frames; glTF transports those frames and editable-part IDs.

entities.name: Input bindings
entities.guidance: Resolve current XRInputSource handedness/profiles and every targetRaySpace/gripSpace pose into one declared base/reference space each frame; targetRaySpace may select, while non-null gripSpace supplies held-object pose.

entities.name: Transform transaction
entities.guidance: Snapshot product transform, a stable source ordering, both hand poses in the common base space, hand separation and an up/fallback frame at grab start; commit only finite one-hand or two-hand product-root transforms.

state_contract.model: Choose one declared base/reference space and resolve every grip pose into it before transform math. One-hand grab stores T_object0 and inverse(T_grip0_in_base)*T_object0, then applies the current grip pose in that same base. Two-hand start requires two distinct tracked sources in a saved stable order, finite common-space grip poses and baseline separation d0>epsilon. Each frame compute midpoint translation and axis a=(p2-p1)/d. Project the saved up reference perpendicular to a; if its norm<=epsilon, try one explicitly saved fallback vector, and if that projection is also ill-conditioned freeze/reject the update rather than create a new basis. Otherwise normalize the projected up, construct the declared handed orientation, and apply scale s=clamp(d/d0,smin,smax) with 0<smin<=smax only to the product root, never camera, reference space or tracking world. If either pose is lost, freeze last valid transform and require an explicit transition to one-hand continuation, cancel-to-snapshot or desktop mode.
state_contract.authority: Blender/glTF owns product hierarchy, origin, metre scale, colliders and handle frames. The user agent owns live XRInputSource/grip poses and profiles. Three.js owns the grab transaction, finite guards, product-root transform, loss policy, undo/reset and modality-independent command mapping.
actions: Use desktop orbit/translate/scale controls with the same bounds.

invariants: Product parts retain local transforms under root manipulation.
Two-hand update is unavailable when d0<=epsilon, current separation<=epsilon, a grip pose is nonfinite/not in the declared common space, or both saved up/fallback projections are ill-conditioned.
Camera/reference space/tracking world is never scaled.
Controller loss, source reordering or orientation degeneracy cannot jump or silently commit a new baseline.
motion_guidance: Pose updates apply from the saved transaction baseline rather than integrating frame deltas, preventing drift; smoothing, if used, is display policy with raw target retained.
creative_affordances: Highlight handles and show a scale ruler/axis without imitating physical force.
known_limits: No controller profile, hand tracking, ergonomics, collision response, headset, render or runtime was tested.

claims.statement: WebXR XRInputSource provides targetRaySpace, optional gripSpace, handedness and an ordered profiles list; input-source objects are live and applications comparing state across frames must copy the relevant values.
claims.scope: WebXR Device API Candidate Recommendation Draft 9 June 2026; the bimanual transform, clamps and loss transition are authored interaction rules.

source_refs.locator: Section 10.1 XRInputSource attributes, profiles ordering and live-object note

object_craft.structure: Blender creates the product root, stable part pivots, handle empties and simplified colliders in metres; glTF exports hierarchy and handles, not controller mappings.
object_craft.material: Hovered/grabbed/second-hand/unavailable handles differ by outline and glyph.
object_craft.articulation: Three.js resolves live grip poses into one declared base space, uses saved source order and a guarded orientation frame, applies the bounded transform to the product root only, handles pose loss and shares actions with desktop controls.

physical_contract.scope: Kinematic product-root inspection transform; no hand force or rigid-body dynamics.
state: declared base space and ordered input-source identities/common-space poses
checks: Zero baseline/current separation rejects two-hand update.
Common-space conversion or both orientation-frame projections failing freezes without jump.
Drop either pose freezes without jump.
Desktop and XR obey identical scale bounds/reset.
